cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: New Rule Required
cards.instruction: Use every problem as justification for adding another rule, ceremony, checkpoint, or layer of oversight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I knocked the teapot twice like you. Now there's tea on the table; we need a rule about tapping.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was knocking on the lid to see whether it was stuck. You hit the spout.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly why we need approved tapping points. I'll mark the lid.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please just use a cloth. The tea's reaching my papers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Cloth first, then. From now on, no papers within a teapot's reach.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copies tapping wrongly and responds with a rule; B2 correction yields A3 marked lid and B4 threatened papers yield A5 a new placement rule.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 lid/spout distinction drives A3 marking; B4 spreading tea makes A5 cloth and papers relevant.

relationship.evidence: B4 wants immediate cleanup, but B2 knocking to see whether a lid is stuck is an awkward account of a real action.

heightening.evidence: A5 accepts B4 cloth while creating a separate paper-exclusion rule.

specificity.evidence: A1 spill and B4 papers are concrete; B2 tapping purpose needs clearer wording.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 cloth first then a rule is concise; A3 approved tapping points is deliberately bureaucratic.
